title: API server: symlinks in `--staticassets` pointing outside the directory return 500

detection.reason: what the `--staticassets` directory contains inside the argocd-server image is not collected

quote: The `--staticassets` directory in the API server (`/app/shared` by default) is now protected against out-of-bounds symlinks. This is to help protect against symlink attacks. If you have any symlinks in your `--staticassets` directory to a location outside the directory, they will return a 500 error starting with 3.1.
remediation: If you ship custom UI assets via a custom image or a mounted volume, replace symlinks that leave the static-assets directory with real files.
verifyCommand: kubectl -n argocd get deploy argocd-server -o json | jq -r '.spec.template.spec.containers[].args[]? | select(test("staticassets"))' # printed = a custom static-assets directory; check it for out-of-bounds symlinks

title: The v1 resource-actions API endpoint is deprecated in favour of `/actions/v2`

detection.reason: API clients that call the resource-actions endpoint are not on the cluster

quote: The `/api/v1/applications/{name}/resource/actions` endpoint is deprecated in favor of `/api/v1/applications/{name}/resource/actions/v2`.
remediation: Move scripts and integrations that run resource actions to the v2 endpoint (parameters in a JSON body) before a later release removes v1; the CLI already falls back on its own.

title: OIDC with PKCE: the authorization code flow moves from the UI to the server — redirect URI changes

detection.reason: `enablePKCEAuthentication` is inside the VALUE of argocd-cm's `oidc.config` key; ConfigMap values are not collected

quote: The server now always handles this flow, PKCE being enabled or not.
remediation: If `oidc.config` sets `enablePKCEAuthentication: true`, add `<argocd-url>/auth/callback` to the OIDC client's redirect URIs at your identity provider before upgrading, or logins fail.
verifyCommand: kubectl -n argocd get cm argocd-cm -o jsonpath='{.data.oidc\.config}' | grep enablePKCEAuthentication # printed true = register /auth/callback as a redirect URI

title: Built-in health checks added for 19 resource kinds — Applications that deploy them can turn Degraded or Progressing

detection.reason: objects of these custom resource kinds, and their current health, are not collected; the hint names the installed CRDs whose group and kind are on the list (group and kind are matched separately, so a CRD pairing a listed group with another listed group's kind is named too) (HTTPRoute and GRPCRoute have their own rule)

quote: * core.spinkube.dev/SpinApp * opentelemetry.io/OpenTelemetryCollector * logstash.k8s.elastic.co/Logstash * kyverno.io/Policy * projectcontour.io/HTTPProxy * grafana.integreatly.org/GrafanaDashboard * grafana.integreatly.org/GrafanaFolder * postgresql.cnpg.io/Cluster * gateway.networking.k8s.io/GRPCRoute * gateway.networking.k8s.io/Gateway * gateway.networking.k8s.io/HTTPRoute * rabbitmq.com/Binding * rabbitmq.com/Exchange * rabbitmq.com/Permission * rabbitmq.com/Policy * rabbitmq.com/Queue * rabbitmq.com/Shovel * rabbitmq.com/User * rabbitmq.com/Vhost
remediation: Objects of these kinds start counting toward their Application's health at this version: one the new check reads as Degraded or Progressing turns its Application Degraded or Progressing and holds later sync waves. Check the status of these objects in the Applications that deploy them before upgrading, or override a kind with `resource.customizations.health.<group>_<Kind>` in argocd-cm.
verifyCommand: kubectl get crd -o json | jq -r '.items[] | select(IN(.spec.group + "/" + .spec.names.kind; "core.spinkube.dev/SpinApp", "opentelemetry.io/OpenTelemetryCollector", "logstash.k8s.elastic.co/Logstash", "kyverno.io/Policy", "projectcontour.io/HTTPProxy", "grafana.integreatly.org/GrafanaDashboard", "grafana.integreatly.org/GrafanaFolder", "postgresql.cnpg.io/Cluster", "gateway.networking.k8s.io/Gateway", "rabbitmq.com/Binding", "rabbitmq.com/Exchange", "rabbitmq.com/Permission", "rabbitmq.com/Policy", "rabbitmq.com/Queue", "rabbitmq.com/Shovel", "rabbitmq.com/User", "rabbitmq.com/Vhost")) | .metadata.name' # CRDs printed gain an Argo CD health check at 3.1 — check the status of their objects in your Applications

title: HTTPRoutes and GRPCRoutes now carry health — a route its parent rejected turns its Application Degraded

detection.reason: names routes whose status reports Accepted=False or ResolvedRefs=False for a parent, which is what the 3.1 route health checks read as Degraded; the check skips a parent whose conditions are from an older generation, and such a route may still be named

remediation: Each route named here reads Degraded from 3.1, and so does the Application that deploys it: a parent Gateway did not accept it, or a backendRef or other reference does not resolve. Fix the parentRefs, the listener's allowedRoutes, or the backendRefs before upgrading, or override `resource.customizations.health.gateway.networking.k8s.io_HTTPRoute` (or `_GRPCRoute`) in argocd-cm.
verifyCommand: kubectl get httproutes.gateway.networking.k8s.io,grpcroutes.gateway.networking.k8s.io -A -o json | jq -r '.items[] | select(any(.status.parents[]?.conditions[]?; (.type == "Accepted" or .type == "ResolvedRefs") and .status == "False")) | .kind + " " + .metadata.namespace + "/" + .metadata.name' # routes printed read Degraded under the 3.1 health checks
